weights.Light: Used for agency identification text and body copy.
weights.Medium: Used for center identification text and headlines.
weights.Bold: Alternative for headlines in certain situations.

secondary_sans_serif.notes: Recommended for its technological character. Requires special attention to size due to small x-height (11pt Futura is comparable to 10pt Helvetica).

primary_serif.notes: Ideal for high quality publications or those of a more permanent nature. Functions well in large volume settings.

secondary_serif.notes: Recommended for newsletters, house organs, and other news-oriented publications.

grid.principle: A predetermined understructure to give a publication cohesive style and character. The grid determines all margins, gutters, and folio placement.

columns.use_case: Small brochures and folders; some educational publications.
News publications, quality publications (to create more movement and flexibility).

spacing.logo_clear_space: A minimum clearance on all sides of three vertical stroke-widths of the logotype is recommended for decals.
element_separation: The NASA Seal and the NASA Logotype should never be used alongside each other.
Mission patches should occupy their own visual space, separated from official NASA identification.

layout_principles: Strive for simplicity, appropriateness, and strength of composition.
Employ a flush left, ragged right format for typography.
The logotype should be shown free-standing horizontally against a solid neutral background.
Language on signage should be clear and concise.

logo.name: The NASA Logotype (The 'Worm')
logo.construction: Letterforms are reduced to their most simplified form with strokes of a single, uniform width. The two 'A' letters lack cross-strokes. For large applications, a grid is provided where 3 grid units equal the vertical stroke width.
logo.reproduction: Must be reproduced photographically from official artwork, not redrawn. Must never be altered or distorted.
forbidden_modifications: Breaking letterforms with a superimposed pattern.
Placing inside a solid or outline shape (e.g., circle, box).
Screening (e.g., benday screen) against a light background.
